title.value: Penalty weight tuning in high dose rate brachytherapy using multi-objective Bayesian optimization
title.justification: The title is explicitly mentioned in the paper details, both at the beginning and within the document.
title.quote:
PAPER

OPEN ACCESS

Penalty weight tuning in high dose rate brachytherapy using multi-objective Bayesian optimization

analysis.description: This paper discusses a method for automating the optimization of treatment plans in high dose rate brachytherapy for prostate cancer using multi-objective Bayesian optimization, thereby improving the efficiency and potentially the effectiveness of these plans.

type.justification: The study involves a practical application of multi-objective Bayesian optimization to actual treatment plan optimization in high dose rate brachytherapy for prostate cancer, using data from 13 patients.
type.quote: This study investigates the weight tuning problem in HDR brachytherapy using MOBO with q-expected hyper-volume improvement (qEHVI) as its acquisition function... Treatment plans for 13 randomly-selected prostate cancer patients were optimized...

name.justification: The paper involves optimizing treatment plans in brachytherapy, which falls under the domain of Medical Physics.
name.quote: Medical Physics Unit, Department of Oncology, McGill University, Montreal, Quebec, Canada

name.justification: The research focuses specifically on optimizing high dose rate brachytherapy, a form of radiotherapy.
name.quote: Interstitial High dose rate (HDR) brachytherapy for the treatment of prostate cancer...

name.justification: The study revolves around using optimization techniques (specifically multi-objective Bayesian optimization) for treatment plan improvement.
name.quote: This study investigates the weight tuning problem in HDR brachytherapy using MOBO with q-expected hyper-volume improvement...

name.justification: MOBO-qNEHVI is described as the model used for finding optimal penalty weights in treatment plans.
name.quote: To automate this process, this study used a multi-criteria approach called multi-objective Bayesian optimization with q-noisy expected hypervolume improvement as its acquisition function (MOBO-qNEHVI).

is_contributed.justification: The model itself (MOBO-qNEHVI) is used within the study for optimization but is not presented as a new contribution or development by the authors.
is_contributed.quote: MOBO-qNEHVI was implemented by Daulton et al (2021) in Ax API (Bakshy et al 2018).

is_executed.justification: The model was actively used in executing the optimization of treatment plans for patients in the study.
is_executed.quote: This study investigates the weight tuning problem in HDR brachytherapy using MOBO with q-expected hyper-volume improvement (qEHVI) as its acquisition function...

is_compared.justification: The performance of MOBO-qNEHVI was measured and compared in terms of acceptance rates and effectiveness in generating clinically acceptable plans.
is_compared.quote: While SCISE could find clinically acceptable plans for all patients, its performance was highly variable...
